However it is possible, though very difficult, to change another person's point-of-view on something. Here are some strategies off the top of my head:

  • Present evidence and let them draw their own conclusions. Let their brains do the thinking with your evidence. I get that you can lead a horse to water but you can't make it drink. Well, you can still lead a horse to water.

  • Don't just barf up a bunch of statistics or anecdotes all at once. Provide evidence over several encounters with someone.

  • Think incrementally. If you can't convince someone that your idea is the greatest thing ever, at least try to convince them that it isn't terrible. Then maybe that it is okay. Then that it is halfway decent. Etc.

  • Feel free to agree with one of their subpoints if it helps you win them over on a larger point.

  • Have credibility and be honest with whomever you are trying to convince, not just in the matter at hand but with other things as well.

These strategies worked well with family members in the recent election. I tried to a much lesser extent with co-workers for obvious reasons. However, it is possible to interject a comment, especially as a rebuttal if they bring something up.
